title: Define your ideal client in one paragraph
when_to_use: You pitch everyone and hear back from no one.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Ask me 5 short questions, one at a time, about my 3 best past clients. Then write a one-paragraph ideal-client profile (industry, size, trigger, budget) in under 80 words.

title: Research a prospect before you pitch
when_to_use: You found a company you want to work with and know little about it.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Here is what I found on [Company]: [Research notes]. List 3 likely problems they have that my services solve, each with its evidence, in under 120 words. Label guesses as guesses.

title: Cold email with one specific observation
when_to_use: You want to email a prospect who has never heard of you.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a cold email to [Contact name] at [Company]. Open with this observation: [Specific observation]. Add one relevant proof point and end with one yes/no question. Under 90 words, no flattery.

title: Follow up on a cold email
when_to_use: Your cold email got no reply after 5-7 days.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a follow-up to [Contact name] about my email from [Date sent] on [Topic]. Add one new useful idea instead of a guilt line. Under 60 words, 3 sentences max.

title: Ask a mutual contact for an intro
when_to_use: Someone you know is connected to a client you want.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a note to [Mutual contact] asking for an intro to [Contact name] at [Company], with the reason: [Why them]. Include a 2-sentence blurb they can forward. Under 100 words, easy to say no.

title: Reply to a posted job (Upwork or job board)
when_to_use: You found a posted project and want a reply that isn't a template.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Job post: [Paste job post]. Write a reply that restates their goal in one line, gives one relevant result and asks 2 scoping questions. Under 120 words. No 'Dear Hiring Manager'.

title: LinkedIn connection note
when_to_use: You want to connect with a decision-maker without pitching.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a LinkedIn connection note to [Contact name], [Their role] at [Company], that mentions [Shared context]. Under 40 words and 300 characters. No pitch, no link.

title: Turn a past project into a mini case study
when_to_use: You need proof for pitches but have no case studies yet.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Turn these notes into a mini case study. Client type: [Client type]. Problem: [Problem]. What I did: [What I did]. Result: [Result]. Use Problem / Approach / Result, under 150 words. Use only the numbers I gave.

title: Write your one-line positioning
when_to_use: You struggle to answer 'So what do you do?'
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write 5 one-sentence positioning lines in the form 'I help (who) get (result) with (service)'. Each under 20 words. Then tell me which is clearest and why, in 2 sentences.

title: Pitch a current client on a new service
when_to_use: A current client could use a service they don't buy from you yet.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Client name] suggesting [New service] because of [What I noticed]. Give a price range of [Price range] and one next step. Under 110 words, no pressure.

title: Reconnect with a quiet past client
when_to_use: A past client hasn't heard from you in 3+ months.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a note to [Client name], whose [Past project] finished [Months ago] months ago. Share one useful idea for them and ask one question. Under 80 words. No 'just checking in'.

title: Offer overflow help to an agency
when_to_use: You want steady overflow work from an agency or studio.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Contact name] at [Agency] offering to take overflow [Service] work. Mention my rate range, usual turnaround ([Turnaround]) and whether I can work white-label. Under 120 words.

title: Build a prospect list with reasons
when_to_use: You have time to prospect but no list.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Suggest 10 kinds of companies in [Region or niche] that fit my ideal client, each with one reason and one public trigger to watch for. One line each, under 25 words per line. Do not invent company names.

title: Subject lines that get opened
when_to_use: Your pitch emails are not being opened.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write 10 subject lines for an email to [Contact name] about [Topic]. Each under 7 words, no clickbait, no emojis, no fake 'Re:'. Name your top 2 in one sentence each.

title: Weekly outreach plan
when_to_use: You want a steady pipeline from a small daily habit.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} I have [Minutes per day] minutes a day for outreach. Make a 5-day plan (Mon-Fri) that mixes cold, warm and follow-up tasks, with a daily target. Under 150 words, as a table.

title: Discovery call questions
when_to_use: A lead booked a call and you want to qualify budget and scope.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Lead: [Company], asking for [What they asked for]. Write 8 discovery questions covering goal, success metric, deadline, decision-maker and budget. One line each, under 20 words per question.

title: Pre-call questions by email
when_to_use: You want a few answers in writing before the call.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Client name] confirming our call on [Call date] and asking 5 short questions to answer beforehand. Under 120 words. Make the questions optional, not homework.

title: Ask about budget without flinching
when_to_use: The lead hasn't mentioned budget and you need a range.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write 3 ways to ask [Client name] about the budget for [Project], each 1-2 sentences, that give my typical project range as an anchor. Plain words; no 'whatever works for you'.

title: Summarize a discovery call
when_to_use: You just finished a call and your notes are a mess.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Notes from my call with [Client name]: [Paste notes]. Summarize as Goal, Must-haves, Nice-to-haves, Deadline, Budget, Open questions. Under 180 words. Mark anything not in my notes as 'unknown'.

title: Recap email after the call
when_to_use: You want the client to confirm what you heard before you quote.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a recap email to [Client name] from these notes: [Paste summary]. List what I heard in 4-6 short points, then ask them to confirm or correct by [Reply by date]. Under 150 words.

title: In scope / out of scope list
when_to_use: You are about to quote and need clear boundaries.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Project: [Project description]. Write an In scope list and an Out of scope list (5-8 items each) and state the number of revision rounds: [Revision rounds]. Under 200 words.

title: Spot red flags in a brief
when_to_use: Something about a lead feels off.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Brief: [Paste brief]. List up to 5 red flags (vague scope, unpaid test, rushed deadline, no decision-maker), quote the line that shows each, and give one question to ask. Under 150 words.

title: Turn a vague brief into questions
when_to_use: The brief is one line, like 'we need a new website'.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} The brief from [Client name] says: [Paste brief]. Write 6 questions that turn it into a project I can scope (pages, content, deadline, who approves, budget). Under 110 words.

title: Offer a paid scoping session
when_to_use: The project is too fuzzy to quote and you want to be paid to scope it.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email offering [Client name] a paid scoping session for [Fee]: what they get ([Deliverables]), how long it takes, and whether the fee counts toward the project: [Credit terms]. Under 120 words.

title: Find the real deadline
when_to_use: The client says 'ASAP' and you need an actual date.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short reply to [Client name] asking what happens on which date (launch, event, board meeting) so we can set a real deadline for [Project]. Under 70 words, 3 sentences max.

title: Ask who signs off
when_to_use: Several people join the calls and you don't know who approves.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write 2 polite ways to ask [Client name] who gives final approval on [Project] and how feedback will be merged into one list. Each under 50 words.

title: Kickoff assets checklist
when_to_use: You need logins, files and content from the client before you start.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} For [Project], list the assets I need from [Client name] (files, access, content, contacts) as a checklist due [Assets due date]. Add one line: the timeline starts when the assets arrive. Under 150 words.

title: Decline a bad-fit lead kindly
when_to_use: The lead doesn't fit your services, budget or values.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a kind email declining [Client name]'s project. Reason: [Reason it's not a fit]. If useful, suggest [Referral or resource]. Under 80 words, no long excuses.

title: Estimate hours by task
when_to_use: You want a sanity check on effort before you price.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Break [Project description] into tasks and give a low and a high hour estimate for each, plus totals. As a table, under 150 words. Flag tasks where you are guessing.

title: Score the lead before you write a proposal
when_to_use: You want to decide if a proposal is worth your time.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Score this lead 1-5 on budget fit, scope clarity, decision speed and fit with my services, using: [Paste notes]. One sentence per score, then go or no-go. Under 100 words in total.

title: Proposal outline in 6 sections
when_to_use: You have call notes and need a proposal skeleton.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Using [Paste call summary], outline a proposal for [Client name]: Goal, Approach, Deliverables, Timeline, Investment, Next step. 2-3 short points per section, under 200 words.

title: Three-tier quote
when_to_use: You want the client to choose how to work with you, not whether.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Build 3 options for [Project]: Essential at [Price A], Recommended at [Price B], Complete at [Price C]. Say what each tier adds, under 150 words. Recommend the middle tier in one sentence.

title: Opening that mirrors their goal
when_to_use: Your proposal starts with 'About me' and loses the reader.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write the opening paragraph of a proposal to [Client name]. Restate their goal ([Their goal]) and the cost of not solving it ([Cost of waiting]) in their words. Under 70 words, no 'I am excited'.

title: Deliverables with 'done when' lines
when_to_use: You want 'done' to be clear before you start.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} For [Project], turn [Deliverables] into a numbered list where each item has a format, a quantity and a 'done when' line. Include [Revision rounds] revision rounds. Under 160 words.

title: Timeline with client deadlines
when_to_use: Your dates slip because the client is late with feedback.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Make a timeline for [Project] starting [Start date], with my milestones and the client's feedback deadlines. Add one line: if feedback is late, the timeline moves by the same number of days. Under 150 words.

title: Payment terms section
when_to_use: You want deposit and due dates in the proposal, not after it.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write payment terms for [Project] at [Total price]: [Deposit %] deposit to start, balance due [Payment days] days after delivery, how to pay, and that late payment follows our agreement. Under 100 words.

title: Explain the price as value
when_to_use: Your price looks big next to cheaper freelancers.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short 'Why this investment' section for [Client name] that links [Total price] to [Business outcome] and to my proof points. Under 90 words. No invented ROI numbers.

title: Follow up on a sent proposal
when_to_use: You sent a proposal 3 days ago and heard nothing.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a follow-up to [Client name] on the proposal I sent [Date sent] for [Project]. Say I'm holding the [Start date] start until [Hold until], and offer a yes/no reply or a 15-minute call. Under 80 words.

title: One-email proposal for a small job
when_to_use: The job is small and a full proposal is overkill.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a one-email proposal for [Project] at [Price]: what I'll do, what I need from the client, dates, price and how to accept. Under 180 words, plain text.

title: Statement of work summary
when_to_use: The client said yes and you need a short statement of work.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Turn this accepted proposal into a statement-of-work summary for [Client name]: [Paste proposal]. Sections: Deliverables, Out of scope, Timeline, Payment, Change requests. Under 220 words.

title: Price your add-ons in advance
when_to_use: You want upsells priced before the client asks for them.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} For [Project], suggest 5 add-ons a client like [Client name] may ask for later, each with a one-line description and a price in my currency based on my rates. Under 120 words.

title: Answer 'can you send examples?'
when_to_use: The lead asks for samples and only a few of yours fit.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a reply to [Client name] sharing [Sample links or names], with one sentence on why each fits [Their project]. Under 100 words. Do not offer free spec work.

title: Quote a rush job
when_to_use: The client needs it faster than your normal timeline.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a quote note for [Client name]: standard timeline [Normal timeline] at [Price], or rush timeline [Rush timeline] with a [Rush fee %] rush fee, plus what the client must deliver by when. Under 120 words.

title: Turn 'let me think about it' into a next step
when_to_use: The client is interested but stalling.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] replied: [Their words]. Write a reply that asks what is left to decide and offers 2 next steps (a short call or a smaller first phase). Under 90 words, no pressure.

title: Review a proposal before you send it
when_to_use: Before you hit send on any proposal.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Review this proposal: [Paste proposal]. Find vague deliverables, missing dates, missing payment terms and anything I promised without a limit. List the fixes in under 150 words.

title: Reply to 'can you do it cheaper?'
when_to_use: The client likes the proposal but asks for a lower price.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] asked for a lower price on [Project], quoted at [Price]. Write a reply that keeps the price and offers a smaller scope at [Lower option price] instead. Under 100 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: 'Our budget is only half'
when_to_use: The client's budget is far below your quote.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] has [Their budget] for a project I quoted at [Price]. Write a reply showing what their budget buys (a phase or fewer deliverables) and what it leaves out. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Raise your rates for current clients
when_to_use: You are raising rates and need to tell current clients.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a rate-increase email to [Client name]: new rate [New rate] from [Effective date]; work booked before then stays at the old rate. Thank them in one sentence. Under 110 words, no apology. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Answer 'what's your hourly rate?'
when_to_use: A lead asks for an hourly rate and you price by project.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a reply to [Client name] explaining that I price [Project type] by project, giving my typical project range and offering a quote after a 15-minute call. Under 80 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Reply to 'someone quoted less'
when_to_use: The client says another freelancer is cheaper.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] says another freelancer quoted [Competitor price] against my [Price]. Write a calm reply naming 2 differences in what's included, and wish them well if price decides. Under 100 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: 'Cheaper now, more work later'
when_to_use: The client promises future projects in exchange for a lower price now.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] offers future work if I lower my price on [Project]. Write a reply that keeps today's price and offers [Volume terms] only once a second project is signed. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Value-based price check
when_to_use: You want to sanity-check a price against the client's value.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Project: [Project] for [Client name]. Likely value to them: [Value estimate]. My hours: [Hours]. Suggest a price range with your reasoning, using only my numbers. Under 120 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Price a new service
when_to_use: You are adding a service and don't know what to charge.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} I want to offer [New service]. Using my current prices and these market prices: [Market reference prices], suggest a starter and a full price with what each includes. Under 120 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Say no to a free test project
when_to_use: The client wants free sample work before hiring you.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] asked for a free test of [Task]. Write a friendly reply that offers past samples or a paid trial at [Trial price] instead. Under 80 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Pushback on your payment terms
when_to_use: The client wants net 60 or no deposit.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] asked for [Their requested terms] instead of my terms: [My terms]. Write a reply that keeps my terms and gives the reason in one sentence. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Cut scope, not your rate
when_to_use: The client needs a lower number and you want to stay profitable.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} For [Project] at [Price], list 3 ways to reach [Target price] by removing scope (fewer pages, rounds or features), with what each removes. Under 120 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Yearly rate review
when_to_use: Once a year, to decide your next rate.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} My year: [Hours billed] hours billed, [Revenue] revenue, [Hours unbilled] unbilled hours, demand: [Demand notes]. Tell me whether to raise rates, by how much and for which clients first. Under 150 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Reply to a lowball offer
when_to_use: A lead offers a fee well below your range.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] offered [Their offer] for [Project]. Write a short reply with my starting price for this ([My starting price]) and a polite exit if that doesn't fit. Under 70 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Offer a nonprofit rate on your terms
when_to_use: You choose to give a nonprofit rate and want it framed clearly.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a quote note to [Client name] showing the full price [Price], my nonprofit rate [Nonprofit price], and that the rate applies to this project only. Under 80 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so, beyond this rate.

title: Words for 'that's too expensive' on a call
when_to_use: You need something to say live, not an email.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Give me 4 short spoken replies to [Their objection] for [Project] at [Price]: a question, a scope option, a value line and a polite walk-away. Each under 25 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: 'Can you just add one more page?'
when_to_use: The client asks for something small that isn't in the scope.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] asked me to add [New request] to [Project]; it is outside the agreed scope. Write a reply that welcomes it as a change request at [Change price] and [Extra days] extra days. Under 100 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Change request in writing
when_to_use: The client wants changes and you need them approved in writing first.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a change-request note for [Project]. Change: [Change description]. Price: [Change price]. New delivery date: [New delivery date]. Ask [Client name] to reply 'approved' before I start. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Late feedback moves the timeline
when_to_use: The client was late with feedback but expects the original date.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name]'s feedback on [Deliverable] was due [Feedback due date] and came [Days late] days late. Write an email: the timeline moves by [Days late] days to [New delivery date]; invoice due dates do not change. Under 100 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: One more revision round
when_to_use: The included revisions are used up and the client wants more.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] wants another revision of [Deliverable]; the [Revision rounds] included rounds are used. Write a friendly reply offering an extra round at [Revision price]. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: New stakeholder wants to redo approved work
when_to_use: Someone joins late and wants to change what was already approved.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [New person] at [Company] wants to change [Approved item], which [Client name] approved on [Approval date]. Write a reply: changes to approved work are a change request with a new price and timeline. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: The client is late with content
when_to_use: You can't start because copy, images or access haven't arrived.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} I'm waiting on [Missing assets] from [Client name], due [Assets due date]. Write a reminder: the timeline starts when they arrive, and the payment due date stays as agreed. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: 'While you're at it...'
when_to_use: The client slips a new task into an email about something else.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} In an email about [Current task], [Client name] also asked for [Extra task]. Write a reply that answers the main point, then quotes the extra task separately at [Price]. Under 100 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Prepaid hours for small requests
when_to_use: Small requests keep coming and you want a simple system for them.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Client name] proposing a prepaid block of [Hours] hours at [Hourly rate] for small requests, used in [Minimum increment] steps and reported monthly. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Hold the line on a live call
when_to_use: A new ask comes up on a call and you need words in the moment.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Give me 4 short spoken lines for when [Client name] adds [New request] on a call: note it, say it's outside the scope, promise a price by [Quote by date]. Each under 20 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Reset scope after a messy month
when_to_use: The project drifted and you need to restate what's in and out.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} For [Project], write an email to [Client name] restating the original scope ([Original scope]), listing extras done so far ([Extras so far]) and how extras are billed from now on. Under 140 words, calm. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Bill for extras you already did
when_to_use: You did extra work without a price and want to bill it fairly.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} I did [Extra work] for [Client name], outside the scope, about [Hours] hours. Write an email explaining a one-time invoice of [Amount] due [Due date], and that future extras get a quote first. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: The client wants a new direction
when_to_use: Halfway through, the client wants a different concept.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] wants to switch [Project] from [Old direction] to [New direction]. Write a reply: work to date is billed at [Amount to date], and the new direction gets a new quote and a new timeline. Under 120 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Merge scattered feedback into one list
when_to_use: Feedback arrives in comments, emails and chat messages.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Scattered feedback on [Deliverable]: [Paste feedback]. Merge it into one numbered list, flag conflicts and out-of-scope items, and draft 2 sentences asking [Client name] to confirm. Under 180 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: The deadline moves earlier
when_to_use: The client wants the delivery date pulled forward.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] wants [Project] by [Earlier date] instead of [Original date]. Write a reply with 2 options: the original date, or the earlier date with a [Rush fee] rush fee and this reduced scope: [Reduced scope]. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Close the project, open the next one
when_to_use: The project is done but 'quick' requests keep coming.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Project] for [Client name] was delivered [Delivery date]. Write an email confirming it is complete, that support ended [Support end date], and how to book new work (a quote or a retainer). Under 100 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Ask for the deposit before you start
when_to_use: The client said yes, but the deposit invoice hasn't been paid.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short email to [Client name]: we start [Start date] once the [Deposit %] deposit ([Amount]) on invoice [Invoice #] is paid; if it arrives later, the start date and timeline move by the same days. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Friendly nudge before the due date
when_to_use: An invoice is due in a few days and you want it paid on time.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a 3-sentence reminder to [Client name] that invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] is due [Due date], with the payment link [Payment link]. Warm, no apology, under 60 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.
check_2: Due date is a real date

title: First reminder: invoice 14+ days late
when_to_use: The due date has passed and your nudge got no reply.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a payment reminder to [Client name] at [Company]. Invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] was due [Due date] and is [Days overdue] days overdue. Ask them to pay this week via [Payment link]; late payment is handled under the terms in our agreement. Under 120 words, one clear ask, no apology. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.
check_3: One date, one way to pay

title: Pause work until the invoice is paid
when_to_use: An invoice is overdue and the client wants the next piece of work.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Client name]: I'll start [Next deliverable] once invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] is paid. The timeline moves by the days the payment is late; the invoice due date does not change. Under 100 words, calm. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Second reminder: a month late
when_to_use: The first reminder didn't work and the invoice is now a month overdue.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a second reminder to [Client name]: invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount], due [Due date], is [Days overdue] days overdue. Ask for payment by [Pay by date] or a call to agree a date, and say late fees apply per our agreement. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: 'Payment is in process'
when_to_use: The client says it's with accounts, but nothing arrives.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] said invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] is 'in process'. Write a reply asking for the expected payment date and the name of the person in accounts. Under 70 words, 3 sentences max. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: The client asks to pay in installments
when_to_use: The client can't pay the full invoice at once.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] asked to split invoice [Invoice #] ([Amount]) into installments. Write a reply proposing [Number of payments] payments on [Payment dates], agreed in writing, with work paused if one is missed. Under 110 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Final notice before a late fee
when_to_use: The invoice is long overdue and your agreement has a late fee.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a final notice to [Client name]: invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] was due [Due date]. If it is unpaid by [Final date], a late fee of [Late fee] applies under our agreement. Under 100 words, firm and factual. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Send an invoice that gets paid
when_to_use: You are sending an invoice and want it paid without a chase.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write the email that goes with invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] to [Client name] for [Project]. Include the due date [Due date], how to pay ([Payment link]) and who to contact. Under 80 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.
check_1: Due date is a real date

title: Ask how the client pays invoices
when_to_use: You are starting with a new client and don't know their payment process.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short email to [Client name] asking who receives invoices, whether a PO number is needed and when their payment runs are, before I send invoice [Invoice #]. Under 80 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Write to accounts payable directly
when_to_use: Your contact is slow and you have an accounts payable email.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Accounts contact] at [Company] about invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount], due [Due date], approved by [Client name]. List the invoice details in 3 lines and ask for the payment date. Under 90 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Thank them for paying
when_to_use: The client paid and you want to keep the relationship warm.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short thank-you to [Client name] confirming payment of [Amount] for invoice [Invoice #] and naming the next step: [Next step]. Under 60 words, no comment on how late it was. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: The client paid the wrong amount
when_to_use: The client paid less than the invoice total.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] paid [Amount received] on invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount]. Write a reply that thanks them and asks for the remaining [Balance due] by [Due date] via [Payment link]. Under 80 words. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Final files after the final payment
when_to_use: Your agreement says final files are released once the final invoice is paid.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Client name]: [Project] is done, previews are attached, and the final files are released once invoice [Invoice #] for [Amount] is paid, as our agreement says. Under 90 words, friendly. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Better payment terms for next time
when_to_use: A client paid late and you want firmer terms in your next contract.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Draft plain-English payment terms: [Deposit %] deposit, balance due [Payment days] days after delivery, late fee [Late fee], work paused after [Pause after days] days overdue. Under 120 words. I will check it locally; this is not legal advice. Do not offer discounts or extra work unless I say so.

title: Delivery email that leads to approval
when_to_use: You are delivering work and want a clear yes or one feedback list.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a delivery email to [Client name] for [Deliverable]: what's included, how to review it, one combined feedback list by [Feedback due date], and which revision round this is: [Revision round]. Under 120 words.

title: Ask for specific feedback
when_to_use: Clients reply 'looks good?' or 'make it pop'.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write 5 specific feedback questions for [Client name] about [Deliverable] that lead to clear yes/no or A/B answers. Under 90 words.

title: Reply to harsh feedback
when_to_use: The feedback stings and you want a calm reply.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Feedback from [Client name]: [Paste feedback]. Write a calm reply that thanks them, restates the 2-3 actionable points and proposes next steps with a date. Under 120 words. No defensiveness, no over-apologizing.

title: Turn vague feedback into tasks
when_to_use: The feedback is fuzzy and you need a to-do list.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Turn this feedback on [Deliverable] into concrete tasks: [Paste feedback]. For each vague item, write one clarifying question. Under 150 words, as a list.

title: Ask for final approval in writing
when_to_use: The last round is done and you need a written sign-off.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email asking [Client name] to confirm final approval of [Deliverable] by replying 'approved' by [Approval by date], and say what happens next (files, invoice). Under 90 words.

title: Handover notes
when_to_use: You are handing over files, logins or a system.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write handover notes for [Client name] on [Project]: what's delivered, where the files live ([File location]), how to use or update them and who to contact. Under 200 words, with headings.

title: Ask for a testimonial
when_to_use: The client is happy and the project just ended.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short email asking [Client name] for a 2-3 sentence testimonial about [Project], with 3 guiding questions (the problem, what changed, would they recommend me). Under 100 words. Make it easy to say no.

title: Turn client praise into a testimonial draft
when_to_use: The client praised you in an email and agreed to a testimonial.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Turn these words from [Client name] into a 2-3 sentence testimonial draft for their approval, keeping their meaning and numbers: [Paste their words]. Under 60 words. Do not add claims they didn't make.

title: Ask a happy client for a referral
when_to_use: The project went well and you want one introduction.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email asking [Client name] if they know one [Type of company] that needs [Service], with a 2-sentence blurb they can forward. Under 100 words. One ask, easy to ignore.

title: Project wrap-up notes
when_to_use: The project ended and you want the lessons on record.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short wrap-up note to [Client name] for [Project]: 3 things that went well, 1 thing to improve next time and one idea for what's next. Use only facts from: [Paste notes]. Under 150 words.

title: You are going to miss a deadline
when_to_use: You will miss a date and need to say so early.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} I will miss the [Original date] date for [Deliverable]. Write an email to [Client name] with the honest reason in one sentence, the new date [New date] and what they get in the meantime. Under 90 words.

title: The client is unhappy with the result
when_to_use: The client says the work isn't what they expected.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] is unhappy with [Deliverable]: [Their complaint]. Write a reply that asks 3 questions to pin down the gap against the agreed brief and proposes a call. Under 120 words. No refund or free work in this email.

title: Portfolio write-up
when_to_use: You want to add a finished project to your portfolio.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a portfolio entry for [Project] for a [Client type]: challenge, approach and result ([Result]). Under 120 words. May I name the client? [Can name client: yes or no]. If no, keep them anonymous.

title: Thank-you note that invites the next project
when_to_use: The final invoice is paid and you are wrapping up.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a thank-you email to [Client name] closing [Project], with one specific thing I enjoyed and an open invitation for [Next service] in [Season or month]. Under 80 words, no hard sell.

title: Six-month check-in
when_to_use: Half a year after a project, to see how it is performing.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a check-in to [Client name] six months after [Project], asking how [Metric] has moved and offering a 20-minute review. Under 80 words, 3 sentences max.

title: Pitch a retainer to a repeat client
when_to_use: A client has hired you 2-3 times and the work repeats.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email to [Client name] proposing a monthly retainer for [Recurring work]: [Monthly scope] for [Monthly fee], billed in advance, with [Notice period] notice to change it. Under 130 words.

title: Retainer scope with limits
when_to_use: You want a retainer that doesn't turn into 'unlimited'.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write the scope section of a [Monthly fee] monthly retainer for [Client name]: included items with monthly quantities, response time, what rolls over (or not) and how extras are quoted. Under 160 words.

title: Renewal email
when_to_use: A retainer or contract ends in about 30 days.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a renewal email to [Client name]: the term ends [End date], highlights from this term ([Highlights]) and the renewal terms ([Renewal terms]). Ask for a yes by [Reply by date]. Under 130 words.

title: Renewal with a higher fee
when_to_use: You are renewing and your fee goes up.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a renewal email to [Client name] with the new monthly fee [New fee] (was [Old fee]) from [Effective date], and one sentence on the added value. Under 110 words, no apology.

title: Monthly retainer report
when_to_use: Month end, to show the client what they got.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Turn these notes into a monthly report for [Client name]: [Paste notes]. Sections: Done, Results, Next month, and usage against [Monthly allowance]. Under 180 words.

title: End a retainer politely
when_to_use: The retainer no longer fits your business.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write an email ending my retainer with [Client name], giving [Notice period] notice from [Notice date], a handover plan and an offer to recommend someone. Under 120 words.

title: The client cancels the retainer
when_to_use: The client tells you they are ending it.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} [Client name] wants to end the retainer. Write a reply that confirms the notice period ([Notice period]) and the last billing date ([Last billing date]), and asks one question about why. Under 90 words, no pleading.

title: Friday admin review
when_to_use: End of the week, 20 minutes, to close loose ends.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Here is my week: [Paste notes on projects, invoices and leads]. Give me a checklist: invoices to send or chase, follow-ups due, and my top 3 priorities for next week. Under 150 words.

title: Plan next week from your calendar
when_to_use: Monday morning, to turn a messy week into a plan.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} My commitments: [Paste calendar and deadlines]. Plan my week in time blocks, with deep work in the mornings and admin in one block. Under 150 words, as a table. Flag overloaded days.

title: Inbox triage
when_to_use: You have a pile of unread client emails.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Here are email subjects and senders: [Paste list]. Sort them into reply today, this week, delegate or ignore, with a one-line reason each. Put money emails first. Under 150 words.

title: Monthly money review
when_to_use: Month end, to see what's paid, owed and coming.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} My numbers: paid this month [Paid this month], invoiced but unpaid [Unpaid], pipeline [Pipeline]. Tell me what to chase, what to invoice and one pricing question to think about. Use only my numbers, under 120 words.

title: Turn a long thread into decisions
when_to_use: An email thread has 25 messages and you need the outcome.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Thread with [Client name]: [Paste thread]. List the decisions made, the open questions and who owes what by when. Under 150 words. Mark anything unclear as 'unclear'.

title: A 30-minute call agenda
when_to_use: Before a client call, so it ends on time with a decision.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a 30-minute agenda for my call with [Client name] about [Topic]: 4-5 items with minutes for each, and the decision we need by the end. Under 80 words.

title: Progress update before there's much to show
when_to_use: Mid-project, the client is anxious and nothing is ready to show yet.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} Write a short progress update to [Client name] on [Project]: what's done, what's next and the date they will see something ([Preview date]). Under 80 words, 4 sentences max.

title: Build your own prompt for a repeat task
when_to_use: You keep doing a task this kit doesn't cover.
prompt: About me: {{profile}} I keep doing this task: [Describe the task]. Write a reusable prompt for it with fields in square brackets, a length limit and 3 checks before sending. Under 150 words.
